en: Coconut oil turns from a clear liquid into a white solid when the temperature drops below 24 degrees Celsius.
Muddy rainwater is a suspension because the heavy soil particles eventually settle at the bottom of a glass.
Galvanized iron roofs in coastal Philippine towns rust faster because salt in the sea air accelerates oxidation.
Making ice candy involves a physical change because the melted juice simply freezes into a solid without forming new substances.
Pumice stones ejected by Taal Volcano float on water because their porous structure makes them less dense than liquid water.
Burning rice husks produces a chemical change because the organic material transforms into ash, smoke, and new gases.
Squeezed coconut milk is an emulsion because tiny liquid fat droplets are dispersed throughout the watery coconut extract.
Sun-drying fish preserves it because the intense tropical heat causes the liquid water inside the meat to evaporate into gas.
The white sand of Boracay beaches is primarily composed of crushed coral, a solid made of calcium carbonate.
Leaving coconut sap in a bamboo tube causes a chemical change as natural yeasts ferment the sugars into alcohol.
Stirring muscovado sugar into hot water causes a physical change because the solid dissolves without altering its chemical identity.
A wooden spoon stays cool in hot sinigang soup because wood is a thermal insulator that conducts heat poorly.
